key_insight: Hot-wire plasma arc WAAM can produce titanium deposits with controlled geometry and high purity when shielding and process parameters are optimized.
engineering_relevance: The study shows a practical route to lower-cost, large-scale titanium part fabrication while revealing direction-dependent properties that designers must account for.
method: Designed a specialized inert-gas shielding system to protect molten titanium from oxidation.
Used full-factorial DOE in Minitab to optimize welding speed, wire current, and wire feed rate.
Verified deposit quality with EDS, 3D microscopy, and mechanical testing in vertical and horizontal build directions.
evidence_signal: The optimized process achieved zero oxygen contamination, UTS values of 560.80–693.58 MPa horizontally and 631.65–677.10 MPa vertically, and hardness ranging from 199.8 to 266.8 HV.
watch_item: The deposited titanium shows anisotropic mechanical behavior and hardness variation along build height, so orientation and layer history must be considered in design and qualification.
paper_title: The process study and parameter influence in Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM) of titanium using hot-wire plasma arc welding
